it regenerates the lock having resolved only a subset of the workspace members. Seen three
times — PR 83 (530→158 packages), PR 96 (→170), and **PR 140 on 2026-08-20 (543→172, only

**A gate DOES catch this now** (this reverses the earlier note in this memory). `repo:publish-metadata`
runs cargo under `--locked`, so a gutted lock reds `moon ci` with:

```
repo:publish-metadata | error: cannot update the lock file <…>/rs/Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to prevent this
```

That one line is the whole signal — `moon ci` otherwise reports only an unattributed
"Tasks: 31 completed, 1 failed", so grep the run log for `--locked` /`publish-metadata`

**How to check** (must use the branch's MERGE-BASE, not current `main` — a stale branch
makes a two-dot diff look like it deletes thousands of unrelated lines):

```bash
mb=$(git merge-base origin/main <pr-head>)
for r in "$mb" <pr-head>; do
  echo "$r: $(git show "${r}:rs/Cargo.lock" | grep -cF '[[package]]') packages, \
$(git show "${r}:rs/Cargo.lock" | grep -cE '^name = "paigasus') members"
done
```

Note the `${r}` braces — in zsh, `"$r:rs/Cargo.lock"` silently applies the `:r` history
modifier and strips the extension, yielding a bogus path and a 0 count.

**How to repair.** Discard the bot's lock and redo the bumps on main's intact one — these
are lock-only changes because `rs/Cargo.toml` declares caret ranges. `--precise` takes only
ONE value per invocation, so loop rather than chaining:

```bash
for spec in "http@1.4.2:1.5.0" "uuid@1.24.0:1.24.1"; do   # from@old:new, one per crate
  cargo update --manifest-path "$WT/rs/Cargo.toml" -p "${spec%%:*}" --precise "${spec##*:}"
done
cargo metadata --locked --manifest-path "$WT/rs/Cargo.toml" >/dev/null   # verify
```

`rand` needs the `rand@0.9.4` disambiguator (0.8.6, 0.9.4, 0.10.2 all coexist). Verify the
net diff vs `origin/main` is exactly 2 lines per crate (version + checksum) and nothing else.

**Deliver the fix as a fast-forward commit on top of the bot's head, not a force-push.**
Force-pushing to the dependabot branch is blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier, and
the plain commit is better anyway — the bot's original stays auditable and the correction reads
as its own diff. Work in a `git worktree` (peers share this checkout, [[paigasus-concurrent-session-branch-clash]]);
`dependabot/*` is allow-listed by the pre-push branch-name hook, but commit-msg still needs
`ts/node_modules` — run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree's `ts/` rather than
`--no-verify` ([[paigasus-commitlint-body-hash-footer-gotcha]]).

**The truncation is not always the only breakage.** PR 149 (`rand` 0.9.5→0.10.2, 2026-08-22)
carried the usual gutted lock (543→176) *and* a genuine breaking-API bump. Don't stop
diagnosing at the lockfile — read the actual compile errors first:

paigasus-iam-rs:lint   | error[E0432]: unresolved import `rand::rngs::OsRng`
```

bumped `rs/Cargo.toml`.

```bash
git -C "$WT" show origin/main:rs/Cargo.lock > "$WT/rs/Cargo.lock"
(cd "$WT/rs" && cargo update --workspace)   # net delta: 2 lines
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked   # --locked proves the lock satisfies the manifest
```

That reduced a +4732/-605 diff to two edges (`paigasus-iam`, `paigasus-observability` moving
